the declines in science enrolment are part of a much broader phenomenon of falling enrolments in traditional subject areas.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the decline in science enrolments in the senior years of high school, and not with science enrolments in general.

the decline in the proportion of students taking physics and chemistry in Year 11 can be understood in terms of the changing context for Year 11 subject choice.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the declines in senior science enrolments are part of a larger phenomenon that has seen declines across many traditional subject areas.
the declining popularity of science subjects is not due to a decline in interest in science per se but to a change in the context of senior school choice.

the declines in the proportions taking physics, chemistry or biology in Year 11 are not due to any particular factor, but rather to a complex set of factors that are part of the broader context of subject choice in senior high school.
